Przasnysz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Przasnysz, Poland

Not demolished. Przasnysz's Jewish community significantly developed after Poland's partitions; by 1921, 2,158 (36%) were forced out by Germans in fall 1939, most later murdered in the General Government. This cemetery, absent from 1781-1783 church visitation records but confirmed by the 1839 Topographic Charter of the Kingdom of Poland, was devastated during WWII - Rabbi Szymon Huberband reported that 'the tombstones were pulled out, the ground was plowed and used as a road.' Poland's local council formally closed the cemetery in 1961, noting no burials had occurred since 1940 and all tombstones had been destroyed by German occupiers; officials considered a park or playground for the site. A 1986 memorial (two steles inscribed 'In memory of those who lived with us') gathered about 30 tombstones from Chorzel, Maków Mazowiecki, and Przasnysz itself.
